recent_posts.title: How to turn an old Android phone into a car diagnostic dashboard
recent_posts.summary: An old scratched Android phone with poor battery life was repurposed as a real-time car diagnostic dashboard using a Bluetooth OBD-II adapter and the Car Scanner ELM OBD2 app. By pairing the adapter to the phone, mounting it on the dashboard, and customizing widgets, the author created a live display showing engine data, coolant temperature, fuel consumption, and more. The setup took about 10 minutes, cost very little, and replaced expensive mechanic visits for basic diagnostics.

recent_posts.title: Four Windows security settings to configure on a new PC
recent_posts.summary: A practical checklist for securing a new Windows PC covering four key areas: running Windows Update and checking the security dashboard, enabling device encryption and saving the BitLocker recovery key, configuring Windows Security features like real-time protection, Controlled Folder Access, and SmartScreen, and setting up automatic screen lock, human presence detection, and Find My Device to prevent unauthorized physical access.

recent_posts.title: PowerToys Grab and Move lets you drag and resize Windows from anywhere
recent_posts.summary: PowerToys' new Grab and Move feature lets Windows users move windows by Alt+left-clicking anywhere on them and resize by right-clicking inside to pull the nearest edge or corner. This eliminates the need to precisely target title bars or window borders. The feature includes an exclusion list for apps that use Alt for their own shortcuts. Corner detection is slightly imprecise but not a dealbreaker. The author notes Linux desktops have offered this for years and questions why Microsoft hasn't shipped it natively.

recent_posts.title: Windows Recall is innovative but privacy concerns will keep most users away
recent_posts.summary: Windows Recall, Microsoft's AI-powered screen-capture and search feature for Windows 11, is technically impressive but faces a fundamental adoption problem: privacy concerns. The feature continuously snapshots your screen and makes your entire PC history searchable using on-device AI, with no data sent to Microsoft's servers. Despite being opt-in, locally processed, and tied to Copilot+ PCs with dedicated AI hardware, most users are unwilling to enable a system that archives all their screen activity. The tool has also had its security cracked at least twice, reinforcing user hesitation. The author argues Recall is one of the most innovative Windows features in years, but its very nature works against widespread adoption.

recent_posts.title: PCIe x1 slots can add modern features to older PCs without a motherboard upgrade
recent_posts.summary: PCIe x1 slots, often overlooked in favor of x16 GPU slots, can add significant functionality to older PCs without requiring a full motherboard upgrade. These small slots support expansion cards for Wi-Fi 6E, extra USB ports, SATA, and capture cards. PCIe x1 cards also outperform common workarounds like USB hubs or M.2 adapters, offering up to 16 Gbps bandwidth on PCIe 4.0 x1 — often more than older USB ports can provide.

recent_posts.title: Zotero-Library-in-Obsidian plugin brings your full reference library into your vault
recent_posts.summary: The Zotero-Library-in-Obsidian plugin integrates your full Zotero reference library directly into Obsidian as a searchable, auto-updating table. It eliminates the need to switch between apps, supports custom column layouts, note templates, highlight formatting, and annotation color-based wrappers. The plugin is not yet in Obsidian's official community list and must be installed via BRAT, making it better suited for power users who do heavy research rather than casual users.

recent_posts.title: Why I use Home Assistant instead of Google Home or Alexa
recent_posts.summary: Home Assistant is presented as a superior alternative to Google Home, Alexa, and HomeKit for smart home enthusiasts who want deep customization and local control. Key advantages include broad device compatibility (including obscure brands, discontinued products, and custom ESP32 builds), powerful automation tools via Node-RED and community blueprints, and a voice assistant pipeline that runs on old Android hardware without cloud dependency. The trade-off is a steeper setup process compared to plug-and-play cloud platforms.

recent_posts.title: 4 VS Code extensions worth using alongside Claude Code
recent_posts.summary: A non-developer shares four VS Code extensions they rely on as a Claude Code user. The list includes the official Claude Code for VS Code extension (which provides inline diffs and context-aware prompting), Cline (an open-source AI coding agent with broad model support and MCP integration), GitLens (for Git history, inline blame, and AI-generated commit messages), and VS Code Pets (a fun virtual pet extension inspired by Claude Code's scrapped Buddy feature).

recent_posts.title: Microsoft is testing a new Windows 11 feature that maxes out your CPU in short bursts to launch apps faster
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft is testing a new Windows 11 feature called Low Latency Profile that briefly maxes out the CPU when launching apps or the Start Menu. According to sources cited by Windows Central, the feature can make apps like Edge and Outlook launch 40% faster and the Start Menu up to 70% faster. It currently runs automatically in Windows Insider builds without user visibility, and sources say battery life and thermal impact should be minimal. The feature is still in early development and may change significantly before an official announcement.

recent_posts.title: Ubuntu's modular opt-out approach to AI sets a standard for other operating systems
recent_posts.summary: Canonical's approach to integrating AI into Ubuntu is being praised as a model for how operating systems should handle AI tools. Key aspects include: using open-source and open-weight models that users can inspect, delivering AI tools as removable Snap packages rather than baked-in components, and carefully vetting what gets included. This contrasts sharply with Microsoft's aggressive Copilot rollout across Windows, which the company has since been walking back. The argument is that Ubuntu's opt-out, transparent, and modular approach respects user autonomy in a way other OS vendors have failed to do.
